title: List-equality check: a list field read through a relationship (record.account.labels == 'a') is judged at no door
body:
repo:objectstack#7 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jTeURPvEm465RcoYEC

Follow-up from #36167 (PR #36207 report 7073202453, S3; restated by the L2 record 7076594662 on PR #36340). Filed by the seat, per the dev's "for the seat to file". Parent: #36167.

## What happens

The list-equality check judges a list-valued field read directly on `record` / `previous`, but not one reached through a relationship. `record.account.labels == 'a'`, where `labels` is a multi-value field on the account, is judged at no door: not by `os validate`, not by the MCP tool, and not by `registerFlow`. It reads as an equality and always answers false at run time.

## Why

`ExprSchemaHint` carries only the subject object's `fields` / `fieldTypes` / `multiValueFields`, with `attachedOnRead` as names only and `traversalHydration` as a boolean. `rootMemberOf` answers only direct members of `record` / `previous`. The hop-target definitions exist only inside lint's own walk (`refuseUndeclaredHopField`, which the MCP tool reaches through `judgeAuthoredSiteExpression`).

## To do (pick one, measured first)

A. Add a lint pass beside `refuseUndeclaredHopField`, which already holds the target definitions, that applies the same list-equality judgment to a hop read. No new producer contract.
B. Add a hint member that carries hop targets' field shapes. This is a producer contract, so its L2 runs on the schema face.
Prefer A unless measurement shows the formula-side check must see it.

## Acceptance

- `record.account.labels == 'a'` is refused with the same code and rewrite as the direct read, at every door the direct read is refused at. A single-value hop field (`record.account.name == 'a'`) is the accepted control.

Blocked-by: #36340

## Grade
p2 · area:build · domain:ui. A silent always-false condition on a supported authoring shape.
